channel.title: Dave Liddament
channel.description: Articles and talks by Dave Liddament

item.title: Type Safe PHP: Leveraging Static Analysis for Robust Code
item.description: Type hints reduce bugs and enable safe refactoring, but PHP's type system has limits. Learn how static analysis bridges the gaps.

item.title: Systems Engineer to Cisterns Engineer
item.description: The bootcamp for software engineers who want to switch to plumbing.

item.title: AI Writes Code. PHPStan Keeps It Honest.
item.description: As AI generates more of our code, custom PHPStan rules keep quality and coding standards in check.

item.title: Rector Beyond Upgrades: Transforming Your Workflow
item.description: Rector is best known for code upgrades, but it can do much more. Learn how to automate repetitive tasks and enforce standards with custom rules.

item.title: A static analysis first approach to RFCs
item.description: Where appropriate should PHP updates start off in static analysis world before becoming part of the PHP language?

item.title: Introducing the InjectableVersion attribute
item.description: Learn how the InjectableVersion attribute ensures that correct interface of class is used in Dependency Injection.

item.title: Introducing the RestrictTraitTo attribute
item.description: Learn how the RestrictTraitTo attribute ensures that traits are used correctly.

item.title: Demystifying Dependency Injection in Symfony
item.description: The Dependency Injection Component is a key part of all Symfony applications. It helps developers write decoupled and maintainable code.

item.title: Introducing the TestTag attribute
item.description: Learn how the TestTag attribute helps with testing.

item.title: Creating Custom PHPStan and Rector Rules (Workshop)
item.description: Full-day workshop covering how to write custom rules for both PHPStan and Rector.

item.title: Introducing the NamespaceVisibility attribute
item.description: Learn how the NamespaceVisibility attribute emulates the missing package visibility modifier.

item.title: Introducing the MustUseResult attribute
item.description: Learn how the MustUseResult attribute can prevent coding mistakes.

item.title: Introducing the Friend attribute (example 1)
item.description: Learn how the Friend attribute can be used to enforce the usage of creational design patterns.

item.title: Introducing the PHP Language Extensions Library
item.description: It's possible to use static analysis to emulate new language features in PHP. This article examines how, and introduces the PHP Language Extension Library.

item.title: Custom PHPStan Rules: Automate Standards and Save Time
item.description: PHPStan increases code quality and reduces bugs. Learn how custom rules amplify these benefits.

item.title: Mastering automated refactoring with custom Rector rules (Tutorial)
item.description: Workshop to create your custom Rector rules

item.title: Elevating Legacy
item.description: This talks through how to do upgrade legacy codebases.

item.title: Adding PHPStan to existing projects: Sell the dream, manage the expectations
item.description: This is the first part of a 4 part series of articles about adding PHPStan to existing projects. First we'll deal with team members who might object.

item.title: Getting the most from static analysis
item.description: Learn how to write code to get the most from static analysis tools, so you reduce the bug count on projects you're working on.

item.title: Using AI to convert PHP engine from C to Rust
item.description: The code that executes PHP is currently written in C. Converting this to Rust offers many advantages. This article talks about work in progress to convert the C code to Rust, using Chat GPT.

item.title: Writing custom PHPStan rules (Tutorial)
item.description: Workshop to create your custom PHPStan rules

item.title: Extending the PHP Language
item.description: Learn how to implement new language features using static analysis.

item.title: Introducing static analysis tools to legacy projects
item.description: Tips on how to use static analysis tools with legacy projects

item.title: SARB version 1 released
item.description: Static Analysis Results Baseliner (SARB) is used to create a baseline of these results. As work on the project progresses SARB can takes the latest static analysis results, removes those issues in the baseline and report the issues raised since the baseline. Learn all about version 1.

item.title: A standard for generics in PHP
item.description: Generics in PHP is already a reality with static analysis. The leading static analysers have largely converged on an unofficial standard. This article proposes the first steps towards a standard.

item.title: PHP Generics Today (almost)
item.description: Many PHP developers would love generics. We might have to wait a while until they come along. This article shows how existing tools can give us the power of generics now (almost).

item.title: PHP Generics Today (almost)
item.description: Many PHP developers would love generics. We might have to wait a while until they come along. This article shows how existing tools can give us the power of generics now (almost).

item.title: Practical Static Analysis
item.description: Static Analysis can drastically reduce the bug count in your codebase. This talk gives practical advice on integrating static analysis into your development workflow.

item.title: Code review and CI in your lunch break
item.description: Code review and CI are vital parts of the modern software development process. It also dead easy to set these up for your project. Find out why and how in this talk

item.title: AssertTrue(isDecoupled("my tests"))
item.description: It's good practice to write decoupled code. That good practice should include minimising the coupling between your test code and the code under test. This talk examines why this is important and how to achieve it.

item.title: Effective Code Review
item.description: There are so many benefits from code review; lower development costs, increased code quality, quick up-skilling and on-boarding of team members. This talk shows you how to get the best out of code review.

item.title: The Git Eureka moment
item.description: Let me share my git eureka moment with you. The moment when suddenly everything git related made sense. We'll delve just below the surface to understand what commits and branch really are. With these concepts cemented we'll look at some of git's more advanced features.

item.title: Beat the bugs, before they beat you
item.description: This talk will show you how to write cleaner code with fewer bugs. And best of all you can apply them the next time you write code.

item.title: Don't be so primitive
item.description: A quick look at Value Objects, what they are, the benefits they offer and why sometimes they should be used instead of PHP's primitive types.

item.title: The Test Suite Holy Trinity
item.description: This talk look at the properties of unit, integration and system tests in terms of what they test, how fast they run and how quick they are to write. Will look at how to get the most out of testing at each of these levels, how best to architect code for testing and where best to make comprises.

item.title: Decoupling with events
item.description: Decoupled code is easier to understand, test and extend. This talk looks at how you can use events for decoupling.

item.title: Code review with Gerrit
item.description: Quick introduction to integrating code review using Gerrit into your workflow.

item.title: Design for testability
item.description: Testing code is difficult right? Not if you design your code with testability in mind. Learn how with this talk.
